forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 1pp to 22%. June 2026 lab confidence remains high (Amodei ~2027, Hassabis ~50% by 2030) and OpenAI's GPT-5.3-Codex was described as 'instrumental in creating itself', a recursive-self-improvement signal. But the resolution bar — a clean credible-lab AGI declaration or 3+ leading researchers stating AGI is achieved — is still unmet and contested, so the move is small.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: near-term insider predictions of a transformative technology arriving within a fixed ~3.5-year window, where insiders carry optimism incentives. Such forecasts resolve YES well under half the time; base ~15-20%.

factors_up.factor: Lab leadership timelines (Amodei 2027, Hassabis ~50% by 2030, Legg ~50% minimal AGI by 2028) sit partly inside the window
Recursive self-improvement signals (model 'instrumental in creating itself') accelerate capability gains

factors_down.factor: Resolution bar (clean credible declaration or 3+ researchers) remains unmet and definitionally contested
Labs tend to avoid formally using the term 'AGI' even as capabilities rise

key_uncertainties: Whether any major lab will formally declare 'AGI' rather than avoiding the term
Whether 3+ leading researchers would publicly converge on 'AGI achieved' before 2030
update_triggers: Revise UP if a credible lab announces AGI or 3+ leading researchers state it is achieved
Revise DOWN if frontier progress visibly plateaus or labs explicitly disavow near-term AGI

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Lowered 3pp to 23%. Fresh 2026 data shows the UK consulting market is still projected to GROW (~5.7% in 2026, ~7.4% in 2027), with AI services the biggest revenue driver. AI is reallocating analyst time rather than collapsing headcount, making a ≥33% revenue/jobs decline by 2030 attributable primarily to AI look less likely, though pressure on the junior-leverage model is real.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: incumbent professional-services sectors facing a major automating technology over ~5 years. Sharp (≥33%) sector-wide contractions inside such windows are historically rare; base ~15%.

factors_up.factor: AI directly substitutes for analyst/junior tasks (data retrieval, coding, drafting) that underpin the billing model
Commentary (e.g. ProMarket) explicitly flags economic consulting's exposure

factors_down.factor: UK consulting market projected to grow through 2026-27, with AI as a revenue tailwind not just a threat
Firms are repricing/reskilling toward judgment work rather than shedding ≥33% of value

key_uncertainties: Whether AI-driven efficiency translates into revenue/headcount decline or into expanded scope and new work
Whether 2+ credible analyses would attribute any decline primarily to AI by end-2030
update_triggers: Revise UP if major economic consultancies announce large AI-driven layoffs or revenue falls
Revise DOWN if sector revenue and employment keep growing through 2027-28

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 1pp to 6%. June 2026 polling has Labour in joint-second/third (~19%) with Reform UK leading clearly (~27%) and the Conservatives level. Labour's position is weak, but the next GE need not arrive until 2029, leaving a long runway for incumbent recovery, which justifies a small upward adjustment for time-horizon uncertainty rather than the polls themselves.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: governing parties polling ~8pp behind the leader at mid-term who go on to win most seats at the next election. This happens a minority of the time but is not negligible given multi-year horizons; base ~15-20%, discounted for the unusually fragmented five-party field.

factors_up.factor: Up to ~3 years until the election allows substantial polling reversion
Fragmented vote (Reform/Con/Grn/LD splitting) can let a ~20% party win pluralities of seats under FPTP

factors_down.factor: Labour currently third/joint-second and ~8pp behind Reform with sinking approval
Sustained Reform lead since mid-2025 shows structural, not transient, weakness

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform's lead holds or fragments as the election nears
How FPTP converts a fractured vote share into seats
update_triggers: Revise UP if Labour recovers to within a few points of the lead
Revise DOWN if Reform's lead widens further or an early election is called

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 1pp to 82%. The longer ~8.5-year window comfortably contains most credible lab and researcher timelines (Amodei ~2027, Hassabis ~50% by 2030, Legg ~50% by 2028), and continued frontier progress plus self-improvement signals in 2026 keep this firmly probable, though definitional and resolution risk caps it well below certainty.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: expert/insider forecasts of transformative AI over a long (~decade) horizon, aggregated across surveys and prediction markets, which cluster majority-probability for AGI-like capability by mid-2030s; base ~60-70%.

factors_up.factor: Most named lab/researcher 50% dates fall inside the window
Sustained capability scaling and self-improvement signals

factors_down.factor: AGI definition/resolution is contested; a formal declaration may lag capability
Possible scaling plateaus, compute/energy or regulatory constraints

key_uncertainties: Whether capability gains continue or hit a plateau before 2035
Whether a recognised 'AGI achieved' declaration materialises even if capabilities arrive
update_triggers: Revise UP if a credible AGI declaration occurs or timelines pull forward
Revise DOWN if frontier progress stalls for an extended period

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 8%. The March 2026 US ODNI Annual Threat Assessment judges that China likely will not invade Taiwan in 2027 and has no fixed timeline, viewing the cost as too high near-term. Blockade/invasion remain planning foci and PLA exercises continue (Dec 2025 blockade drill), but short exercises do not meet the >72-hour blockade/assault resolution bar.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: great-power initiations of major blockade or invasion against a defended territory within a ~3.5-year window. Such events are rare given deterrence and economic stakes; base ~5-8%.

factors_up.factor: Continued PLA modernisation and repeated large-scale exercises around Taiwan
Beijing adjusting expansionist objectives and rhetoric

factors_down.factor: ODNI assesses no near-term invasion plan and no fixed timeline
Leadership prioritises domestic development; war risks derailing it

key_uncertainties: Whether an exercise escalates into a sustained (>72hr) blockade
How US/allied posture and cross-strait politics evolve before 2030
update_triggers: Revise UP on a declared quarantine/blockade, mobilisation, or major escalation
Revise DOWN on visible cross-strait de-escalation or arms-control steps

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Lowered 1pp to 3%. ONS data for May 2026 shows headline CPI stuck at 2.8% (unchanged from April), core CPI rising to 2.6%, and services/transport inflation surging (transport +6.8%, highest since Dec 2022). With only ~6 remaining monthly prints before year-end and inflation sitting ~0.8pp above target with upward pressure, a sub-2.0% reading in any single month looks very unlikely.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: monthly probability that a CPI rate sitting at ~2.8% with sticky/rising core falls below 2.0% within ~6 months absent a demand shock. Historically low; base <10%.

factors_up.factor: A sharp energy or food price drop could mechanically pull headline down
Six remaining monthly readings give several chances

factors_down.factor: Headline flat at 2.8% with core rising to 2.6%
Services and transport inflation accelerating, not easing

key_uncertainties: Whether a sudden energy base-effect or demand collapse emerges before year-end
Whether services disinflation arrives faster than the BoE expects
update_triggers: Revise UP if a monthly CPI print drops sharply toward target
Revise DOWN if inflation stays at/above 2.8% through Q3 2026

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 1pp to 85%. With a 31 July 2026 release and ~5 months of runway to year-end, pre-sales are exceptional — reportedly the best first-day pre-sales in five years (north of $37M) and a top-five all-time presale — signalling a No Way Home-scale opening. $1.5B worldwide remains a high bar (No Way Home reached ~$1.9B), so confidence is strong but not extreme.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: tentpole Spider-Man/MCU sequels with elite tracking. The most comparable prior entry (No Way Home) cleared $1.9B; multiple recent MCU/Spider-Man films exceeded $1B; base for clearing $1.5B given elite tracking ~70-80%.

factors_up.factor: Record-breaking pre-sales and sold-out showings indicate a massive opening
Five-year gap since No Way Home concentrates pent-up demand

factors_down.factor: $1.5B is a tier only a handful of films ever reach; weak legs or reception could fall short
China/international performance for MCU titles has been volatile

key_uncertainties: Opening-weekend magnitude and multiplier (legs) after launch
update_triggers: Revise UP after a record opening weekend with strong holds
Revise DOWN on a soft opening or poor word-of-mouth

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Raised 1pp to 99%. By mid-2026 the combined run-rate already sits around or above $70B: Anthropic disclosed a $47B run-rate as of mid-May 2026 (Series H), while OpenAI was at roughly a $24-25B annualized run-rate in spring 2026. Both are growing extremely fast, so a combined Q4 2026 ARR above $70B is now all but locked in.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: near-term financial thresholds already essentially met by current run-rates and trending strongly upward. Such forecasts resolve YES the overwhelming majority of the time; base >95%.

factors_up.factor: Anthropic alone ~$47B run-rate (mid-May 2026) plus OpenAI ~$24-25B already sums to ~$70B+
Both firms compounding rapidly (Anthropic adding ~$96M annualized/day)

factors_down.factor: Reporting definitions ('ARR' vs 'run-rate') and timing of Q4 disclosures could introduce ambiguity
A severe demand/funding shock could stall growth (low probability)

key_uncertainties: Whether Q4 2026 figures are reported on a comparable ARR basis by credible outlets
Any unexpected revenue reversal in H2 2026
update_triggers: Revise DOWN only if a credible Q4 report shows a combined figure under $70B
Already effectively resolving YES on current trajectory

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 39%. The OBR's March 2026 outlook puts medium-term potential output growth at exactly 1.5% and sees growth averaging ~1.6% only over 2027-2030 as the output gap closes. The 2030s themselves face intensifying demographic drag (slowing labour-supply growth from an ageing population), leaving a decade-average above 1.5% roughly a coin-flip tilted slightly below.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: realised UK decade-average real GDP growth rates. The 2010s averaged ~1.5-2.0% and the 2020s have been weaker; clearing a 1.5% mean across a full decade is achievable but not the central expectation given ageing; base ~40%.

factors_up.factor: OBR sees productivity rising toward 1.0% and growth ~1.6% into 2030
Potential AI-driven productivity upside over a full decade

factors_down.factor: Ageing population slows labour-supply growth to ~0.5%, capping potential at ~1.5%
OBR central potential growth is at, not above, the 1.5% threshold

key_uncertainties: Whether AI/productivity gains materially lift trend growth in the 2030s
Severity of demographic drag and net migration paths
update_triggers: Revise UP on sustained productivity acceleration or upgraded OBR/long-run forecasts
Revise DOWN on entrenched stagnation or downgraded potential-growth estimates
